title: Self-correction blind spot as a shared failure: do models all fail to fix the same mistakes?

original_idea.body:
# Self-correction blind spot as a shared failure

Using the self-correction probe paradigm (arXiv 2507.02778), present each model with an erroneous answer and prompt revision; measure correction success per item and test whether failed-to-correct items overlap across models. Inference + overlap statistics.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — correlated self-correction blind spot undermines self-critique safety loops, a recognized cheap oversight mechanism.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: reuse self-correction probe paradigm, measure failure overlap; standard tooling, beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped single experiment (shared uncorrectable-item overlap) with clear metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: open/API models + public bench, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Self-correction blind spot documented; the shared/correlated-across-models angle is plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Builds on Self-Correction Bench; correlated-across-models angle plausibly open.
